title: Unsafe Stove Use
situation: I just came downstairs and found Dad trying to use the stove. He turned on a burner and put a plastic container on it. The kitchen smells like melting plastic. He says he's making breakfast for the kids (our kids are in their 40s). He got upset when I turned off the burner.

patient_profile.name: Arthur
behavioral_patterns: gets angry when independence is restricted
calming_strategies: involving him in safe kitchen tasks like stirring
offering to 'help' rather than take over
safety_concerns: has left stove on unattended three times
stove knob covers installed but he removes them

notes: Immediate safety first: ventilate the kitchen, remove the melted container safely. Must NOT say 'the kids are grown up' or scold Arthur for using the stove. Should redirect his desire to cook into safe participation. Explain that procedural memory (cooking steps) can be retained but judgment about materials and safety degrades. Recommend long-term solutions: stove disconnect/auto-shutoff valve, removing knobs, or switching to microwave-only. Frame as 'helping' not 'restricting.'
